text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for high blood pressure (hypertension) include healthy lifestyle changes and prescription medications.
snippet_highlighted_words: healthy lifestyle changes and prescription medications

list.snippet: Eat healthy food: Follow a low-sodium diet, like the DASH diet, rich in fruits, vegetables, and low-fat dairy.
Exercise often: Do regular aerobic exercise, such as walking, cycling, or swimming.
Lose extra weight: Shedding pounds reduces the strain on your heart and blood vessels.
Limit alcohol: Drink in moderation, or stop completely.
Quit smoking: Stopping smoking improves your overall heart health.
Manage stress: Find healthy ways to cope with daily stress.

text_blocks.snippet: Doctors often prescribe one or more drugs to control blood pressure. You can learn more about these choices through the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI).

snippet_links.text: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

list.snippet: Diuretics (water pills): Help your body get rid of extra sodium and water.
ACE inhibitors: Keep your blood vessels from narrowing by blocking certain chemicals.
ARBs (Angiotensin II receptor blockers): Block the chemicals that make blood vessels narrow.
Calcium channel blockers: Relax and widen blood vessels by stopping calcium from entering muscle cells.
Beta-blockers: Slow your heart rate and reduce the force of each heartbeat.
